name: Sairee Beach
tagline: The island's main strip of bars, dive shops and cafes
description: A long sandy beach on the west coast backed by one narrow walking lane packed with dive schools, smoothie bars, laundries and beach clubs. Most first-time visitors and short-stay divers base here. Several cafes with reliable fibre make it the default daytime work spot on the island.
bestFor: Nomads who want people to talk to, dive courses on the doorstep and no need for a scooter.
pros: Easy to meet other travellers within a day
cons: Bass from beach bars runs late most nights
The busiest and priciest stretch of the island
Beach lane floods and gets muddy in heavy rain

name: Mae Haad
tagline: The pier village where the ferries and the ATMs are
description: The island's practical hub, built around the ferry pier. Streets hold the banks, pharmacies, hardware shops, the 7-Elevens and the cheapest local Thai kitchens. Long-stay residents choose it for convenience rather than looks, and it is a ten minute walk south along the coast path to Sairee.
bestFor: Longer-stay workers who value banks, groceries and ferry access over a sea view.
pros: Best supply of everyday shops and services
Cheapest local food on the island
Quick ferry access for visa runs
cons: Traffic and ferry crowds around arrival times

name: Chalok Baan Kao
tagline: A calmer bay village in the south of the island
description: A horseshoe bay at the southern end with a handful of restaurants, two dive centres and mostly low-rise bungalows on the hillsides above. It is quiet by 10pm and popular with people staying a month or more. Monthly bungalows here run cheaper than anything near Sairee.
bestFor: Nomads on a monthly stay who want sleep, space and lower rent.
pros: Still has cafes, a gym and dive shops
cons: The bay is shallow and rocky at low tide
Slower nightlife and fewer people around

name: Tanote Bay
tagline: An east-coast snorkelling cove with a handful of resorts
description: A small granite-boulder bay on the east side reached by a steep road across the island's middle. There are only a few resorts, one or two restaurants and clear water straight off the sand. Internet is resort-dependent, so it suits people whose work is mostly offline or async.
bestFor: Solo workers who want near total quiet and swim-out snorkelling.
pros: Some of the clearest water on the island
Almost no crowds outside day trips
cons: Steep access road is dangerous on a scooter in rain
Very limited food and shop choice
Wi-Fi quality varies a lot by resort

name: Hin Wong Bay
tagline: The island's most isolated liveable bay
description: A rocky northeast bay with a couple of small resorts, a dive site offshore and effectively nothing else. The dirt access track is rough and there are no shops, so residents ride into Mae Haad for supplies. Best treated as a retreat rather than a base with everyday errands.
bestFor: Writers and deep-work types who want to disappear for a few weeks.
pros: Extremely quiet, close to zero nightlife
cons: Access track is rough and often impassable in rain
No shops, restaurants limited to resorts
